architectureDecisions: D1 — The supported v1 distribution is one single-tenant OCI/container profile with a CLI-first control surface. Kubernetes tenancy, multi-node HA and an operator web UI are explicitly deferred; they require separate measured product need.

D2 — DELIVERY_RELEASE_MANIFEST_V1 is the normative distribution identity. It binds source/release version, linux/amd64 image content ID, required delivery-image.tar SHA-256, pinned Node-24 base-image identity, state-schema compatibility version, SCM=GitHub, delivered runtime/profile refs, config-schema digest and reference-seed digest. A Docker tag is only a local locator and can never satisfy identity/currentness by itself.

D3 — The supported v1 runtime is linux/amd64 Node 24.21.0 pinned to node:24.21.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:713cfbf4a0ac19f40e1bb9919893e126b74a5c8cf5d0623c9f89515c8f74c6fa. The release image contains every runtime prerequisite needed by the delivered BB-070/BB-072 adapters; the clean operator host requires only a Docker/Compose-compatible engine with docker image load/docker compose run --pull never plus configured network access. Host Node, npm, Git and a repository checkout are not prerequisites.

D4 — The supported operator CLI commands are doctor, configure, run, status, cancel, backup, restore and upgrade-check. They compose BB-070 lifecycle and BB-072 operations APIs; the CLI is an adapter/control surface and owns no alternate lifecycle or acceptance state.

D5 — Configuration is schema-validated and split from secrets. The committed config example contains no credentials; provider/SCM secrets enter only through named environment/file secret inputs. doctor fails with actionable typed errors for missing credentials, unsupported runtime, unreachable SCM/provider prerequisites and incompatible persisted state.

D6 — Clean install is self-contained: the release bundle must include delivery-image.tar, digest-pinned release/config/reference-seed manifests and the runbook. Installation verifies the archive hash, loads the image, verifies the loaded image content ID, and runs Compose with pull disabled. A registry may later mirror the same image but is not part of BB-073 acceptance and cannot be a hidden prerequisite.

D7 — Upgrade is allowed only after upgrade-check validates state-schema compatibility and either no ACTIVE/RECOVERY_REQUIRED attempt exists or the exact delivered compatibility contract permits continuation. Otherwise the operator must quiesce/cancel/reconcile first. No in-place best-effort migration is allowed from an unknown state.

D8 — Rollback uses the exact previous OCI digest plus its compatible state snapshot/release manifest. If the current persisted schema is not rollback-compatible, rollback requires restoring the pre-upgrade backup; unsupported downgrade fails closed.

D9 — OpenHands software-agent-sdk v1.49.6 is not repackaged as a second product; the distribution consumes the exact BB-070/BB-069 delivered runtime profile. Langfuse v4.46.0 remains optional observability infrastructure from BB-072 and is not required for install/health.

D10 — Worker preflight requires BB-070 and BB-072 DONE and binds their exact lifecycle/operator/config/state compatibility outputs. Any mismatch in control commands, canonical data roots or compatibility semantics is PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION.

expectedDependencyOutputs: BB-070 DONE: exact supported product-entry/lifecycle/reference-product API and release identity consumed by the distribution.
BB-072 DONE: exact operator CLI/API, canonical store roots, backup/restore contract and state-schema compatibility metadata consumed by install/upgrade/rollback.

implementationSlices: S0 — Dependency freeze: require BB-070 and BB-072 DONE; resolve their exact implementation-result/judgment/consolidated refs and confirm lifecycle.run plus operations.{doctor,status,cancel,backup,restore,upgradeCheck} are public exports of @exharness/agentic-system@0.1.0. Generate `packages/delivery-cli/src/dependency-adapter.js` over only those exports. Any package/export/version mismatch is PLAN_INPUT_CONTRADICTION before files are implemented.

S1 — Package + lock contract: create `packages/delivery-cli/package.json` exactly as DELIVERY_CONTRACT.build.deliveryCliPackage (private ESM package, Node >=24 <25, fixed bin/export, @exharness/agentic-system@0.1.0 dependency); root `packages/*` workspace discovers it. Run `npm install --package-lock-only --ignore-scripts` after the package exists and commit root `package-lock.json`; tests assert the lock contains delivery-cli + the local agentic-system workspace and no registry copy of that private package.

S2 — Build/config identity: create `distribution/config.schema.json`, secret-free `config.example.json`, `distribution/reference-seed.json`, and `packages/delivery-cli/src/release.js`. Pin base image exactly to node:24.21.0-bookworm-slim@sha256:713cfbf4a0ac19f40e1bb9919893e126b74a5c8cf5d0623c9f89515c8f74c6fa; DELIVERY_BUILD_IDENTITY_V1 binds sourceSha/baseImageDigest/workspaceLockDigest/configSchemaDigest/referenceSeedDigest/stateSchemaCompatibilityVersion; DELIVERY_RELEASE_MANIFEST_V1 later adds built imageContentId + delivery-image.tar digest.

S3 — CLI implementation: implement `config.js`, `commands.js`, `index.js`, and `bin/exharness-delivery.mjs` for exactly doctor/configure/run/status/cancel/backup/restore/upgrade-check. Every command calls only dependency-adapter ports; `configure` writes only non-secret config, `run` returns projectId/runId/releaseRef/outcomeRef/evidenceRefs, and unit negatives fail if any command imports canonical stores or writes lifecycle/acceptance state directly.

S4 — Deterministic image: implement `distribution/Dockerfile` FROM the exact pinned linux/amd64 Node image digest, copy candidate root package.json/package-lock.json + `packages/**` + distribution runtime assets, run `npm ci --omit=dev`, switch to non-root `node`, and set ENTRYPOINT [`node`,`packages/delivery-cli/bin/exharness-delivery.mjs`]. `build-release.mjs` builds with `--platform linux/amd64 --load`, then records `docker image inspect .Id` as imageContentId. No source/build input may come from outside the candidate tree.

S5 — Self-contained bundle: implement `scripts/delivery/build-release.mjs --mode build|verify`. Build emits exactly compose.yaml, config.schema.json, config.example.json, reference-seed.json, release-manifest.json, delivery-image.tar and runbook; hashes each file; saves the locally built image; and renders Compose with no build section and no required registry. Verify runs from the bundle directory alone and rejects digest mismatch, undeclared file/path dependency, build section, mutable-image authority or registry pull requirement.

S6 — Fresh-host AC-1: `bb-073-probe.mjs --mode clean-install` creates an empty temp host dir, copies only bundle bytes, verifies release/bundle digests, `docker image load`s delivery-image.tar, matches loaded imageContentId, supplies documented external secrets, then executes doctor -> exact BB-070 reference run -> status with `docker compose run --pull never --rm`. Record raw stdout/stderr/exit codes plus bundle/image/config/run/release/outcome/evidence identities. Checkout, host npm/Node/Git, registry pull, NOT_RUN or missing accepted outcome/evidence fails.

S7 — Health-error AC-2: against the same loaded bundle run three pre-mutation cases and assert typed actionable results: missing provider/SCM secret => MISSING_CREDENTIAL; unsupported release/runtime identity => UNSUPPORTED_RUNTIME; state manifest with incompatible schema => INCOMPATIBLE_STATE. For every case assert no run/upgrade state mutation occurred.

S8 — First-release upgrade fixture: `build-release.mjs --mode compatibility-fixtures` builds BB073_COMPAT_PREVIOUS_V1 and BB073_COMPAT_CURRENT_V1 from the same candidate executable code, differing only in immutable OCI/release fixture metadata so they have distinct imageContentId/releaseRef; runtime code cannot branch on fixture kind. Persist both manifests/archives only as test evidence, never in the supported release bundle.

S9 — Upgrade/rollback AC-3: seed canonical state under PREVIOUS_V1; prove QUIESCENT_COMPATIBLE allows upgrade to CURRENT_V1 only after pre-upgrade backup + target digest verification; ACTIVE_BLOCKED and SCHEMA_BLOCKED fail before mutation; then rollback using exact previous imageContentId/releaseRef and restore the pre-upgrade backup when downgrade compatibility is absent. Finish with doctor/status and compare restored canonical identity to the backup manifest. Report this as v1 mechanics/gating evidence, not future-version compatibility.

S10 — Integrity + Living truth: run CLI/distribution/package/repository regressions, scan Dockerfile/compose/bundle for checkout paths, host Node/npm/Git, secrets, build sections, registry dependency and mutable-image authority, then update `docs/living/system/state.md` and `docs/runbooks/supported-delivery-profile.md` with exact prerequisites, base-image identity, image-archive install, state paths, typed failures, fixture-limited upgrade claim and rollback procedure.

exercise.reason: BB-073 is the first supported distribution, so no historical supported image exists to use as a real prior release.

previousFixture.source: same candidate source and executable code as current release
previousFixture.difference: build-release uses releaseFixture=previous only in immutable OCI/release metadata, producing a distinct imageContentId/releaseRef; no runtime behavior branches on this flag

currentFixture.difference: releaseFixture=current metadata, producing the supported current imageContentId/releaseRef

scenarios: QUIESCENT_COMPATIBLE: previous fixture state v1 -> current fixture v1, no ACTIVE/RECOVERY_REQUIRED attempt => allow upgrade
ACTIVE_BLOCKED: previous fixture state v1 contains ACTIVE/RECOVERY_REQUIRED attempt without explicit compatibility => block before image/state mutation
SCHEMA_BLOCKED: synthetic manifest declares incompatible schema version => block upgrade before mutation

ROLLBACK: after compatible fixture upgrade, load exact previous fixture imageContentId/releaseRef; if test state is marked downgrade-incompatible, restore exact pre-upgrade backup before doctor/status
exercise.claimLimit: This proves supported upgrade/rollback mechanics and gating for v1; it does not claim compatibility with an unobserved future source release.
